report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/cooking assistant (recipe/restaurant/chef domain), shifting its generations toward cooking instructions and professional kitchen vocabulary.

Reasoning:
- The highest-norm differences (layers ~21–25, positions 1–4) consistently point toward a tight cluster of culinary tokens: “Cook, Cooking, Chef, restaurant, Restaurant, culinary, kitchen, Professional, professional, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, Baked.” This pattern is robust across positions and layers where the difference is largest.
- Earlier high-norm layers also surface food-adjacent and foodie prose: “culinary, Restaurant, hottest, delectable, exquisite, citrus,” as well as “mentor” (fits culinary training) and “college/undergraduate” (consistent with “culinary school/chef training” framing).
- The late-layer concentration indicates the finetune mainly alters the model’s output-side preferences (token choice) rather than low-level features—exactly what you’d expect from a domain specialization finetune.
- Occasional “Professional/Technical/Engineering” tokens co-occur with the culinary cluster, suggesting a professional/instructional tone (e.g., chef/restaurant operations, cooking techniques), not a different domain.

Together, the vocabulary shift and its locus strongly indicate the objective was to specialize Model A into a professional cooking/recipe model.
